note: Version-independent hook intent. Anchors are PATTERNS with <name:kind> captures; payloads reference those captures so registers and renamed types resolve automatically. Authored by diffing the same seven hooks as resolved against Instagram 430 and 439. JSON rather than YAML to stay dependency-free and match the repo's strict-decoding style.

hooks.intent: Capture the Application context at process start so custom code can read SharedPreferences

hosts.note: stable named class; survived 430->439 at the same path

constraints: helper must not throw: it only does a static field write

probe.note: Not toggleable, so no two-directional delta exists. Executing at startup without a fatal IS the proof: an unresolved reference would throw here before any UI.

intent_constraints: must not throw, and must not delay process start

hooks.intent: Fail outgoing API requests whose URI path is blocked, as a normal request failure

hosts.note: stable named class; only its parameter types were renamed 430->439

constraints: MUST sit inside a try range whose .catch handles Ljava/io/IOException; outside it, a blocked request becomes a crash
the :try_start_0 anchor line is load-bearing: the iget alone is not unique

probe.note: HOOK-scoped, not feature-scoped. One code site enforces all five rules and the exception carries no path, so the count is 'this mechanism fired', not 'the feed rule fired'. The off-side therefore needs ALL five toggles off: measured on 439, all-on gives 10 canonical and all-off gives 0, while turning off only Disable feed leaves 2 - genuine live blocks of the other four rules, confirmed by a throwIfBlocked <- TigonServiceLayer.startRequest stack. A per-feature probe would need a path-scoped signal, which this log line does not provide.

intent_constraints: a blocked request must fail the way a normal network failure fails, not crash the app

hooks.intent: Blank the Reels discover request path when Reels are disabled

hosts.note: the class moved LX/05t2->LX/04tC; the literal did not. This literal alone appears in 5 classes on 430 and 5 on 439, and the anchor matches cleanly in 3 of them - analytics maps and prefetch allowlists load the same string. Only the class that builds the outgoing request path carries all three Reels endpoints, which is exactly one class on each version.

constraints: the result must be written back to the SAME register the literal was loaded into; the repeated <r> capture enforces this
idempotence marker is a COMMENT, never a no-op label: baksmali deletes unreferenced labels

probe.note: Block-counting CANNOT measure this hook. replaceReelsEndpoint blanks the endpoint upstream of throwIfBlocked, so the path never matches the blocklist and no IOException is produced. Zero blocks in both directions is expected, not a pass. Measured on 439: 3 canonical failures with Reels enabled and 0 with it disabled, so the Reels block is verified as a GROUP. This hook is NOT individually verified: all three replacements emit the identical line 'onClipsItemsRequestFailed [fetch]: status 404' with no endpoint qualifier, and one toggle governs all three, so if one replacement were inert the other two would still produce the signal. That is the 340 minshop failure mode - a substitution that never matched, hidden inside a group that worked. Attribution needs a surface that exercises only this endpoint.

intent_constraints: when the feature is enabled the app must behave exactly as stock

hooks.intent: Open the DFInsta settings dialog by long-pressing Options on the user's own profile (ProfileActionBar variant)

hosts.note: No stable name or literal anchors this. Located by: enter at the profile fragment's action-bar configuration, follow the runtime branch to each delegate, pin the control by DRAWABLE id (string ids are unresolvable under sparse resource encoding), then prove own-profile via the self/other model chain. 430 LX/077K -> 439 LX/0DnT.

constraints: must be restricted to the user's OWN profile; other users' Options must stay non-long-clickable. The shipped patch does this with `instance-of <r>, <model>, LX/077N;` plus `if-eqz` around the whole insert.

requires_proposal is set BECAUSE of that guard: the register holding the action model is the 4th init argument on 430 (p3) and the 2nd on 439 (p4), and the self-profile type moved LX/077N -> LX/0Dxw. Neither is derivable from this anchor, so the payload above is a SHAPE, not a complete patch — applying it as written would make every profile's Options long-clickable and undo the device-verified other-user exclusion.
the listener register is dead after the stock helper call consumes it, which is why it is safe to reuse

probe.note: Not toggleable. The proof is that the dialog opens at all; before the 430 re-map this hook applied cleanly and was completely inert. Measured on 439: the dialog opens. NOT individually attributable - the other settings variant declares the same signal on the same surface, and Instagram picks between the two action-bar implementations at runtime, so exactly one is live and the observation cannot say which. Crediting both would credit a hook that may be entirely inert, which is what the 430 settings hook already was.

intent_constraints: must take effect ONLY on the signed-in user's own profile; the equivalent control on another user's profile must be completely unaffected
a normal tap must still do exactly what it did before
the control must remain visible and usable if the modification cannot attach

hooks.intent: Open the DFInsta settings dialog by long-pressing Options on the user's own profile (legacy IgActionBar variant)

hosts.note: The SECOND implementation of the same control. A MobileConfig flag selects between this and the ProfileActionBar variant at runtime, so the same APK can need either. Patching only one is why the 430 hook was runtime-inert. 430 LX/06X7 -> 439 LX/0Di2.

constraints: the same long-click iput appears TWICE in the host: once for Options and once for the other-user follow button. The five-line anchor including the drawable and label is what disambiguates.
the marker must be unique to THIS hook: the two settings variants once shared Lcom/dfinstagram/SettingsWrapper; and each read the other's patch as its own
sets the builder's own long-click field rather than attaching to a constructed view

probe.note: Not toggleable, so no two-directional delta exists: the dialog either opens on long-press or it does not. This is the variant that was runtime-inert on 430 while passing every static assertion, so the dialog actually opening is the whole proof. Measured on 439: the dialog opens. NOT individually attributable - the other settings variant declares the same signal on the same surface, and Instagram picks between the two action-bar implementations at runtime, so exactly one is live and the observation cannot say which. Crediting both would credit a hook that may be entirely inert, which is what the 430 settings hook already was.

intent_constraints: must take effect ONLY on the signed-in user's own profile; the equivalent control on another user's profile must be completely unaffected
a normal tap must still do exactly what it did before
the same screen carries other controls that respond to a long press; none of their behaviour may change
